description: Unify server JSON serialization behind a single facade with a non-ASCII-preserving encoder, wire it into HTTP and SignalR global options, and converge all scattered business-code options so Chinese (and other non-ASCII) text stops being serialized as \uXXXX escapes.

tasks.title: Establish unified JSON facade with non-ASCII encoder and converter ownership
tasks.spec: specs/json-serialization/spec.md#Unified options preserve non-ASCII characters via a safe encoder
tasks.description: Enhance the existing Mohist.Server.Infrastructure.JSON facade: add Encoder = JavaScriptEncoder.Create(UnicodeRanges.All) to JSON.Options, add a read-only Indented variant (JSON.Options cloned with WriteIndented = true), and promote the options-scoped UnknownFailureReasonJsonConverter out of WorkflowQuerier into a shared/internal converter registered once on JSON.Options. This makes the facade the single source of JsonSerializerOptions and the single correct entry point for serialize/deserialize.
acceptanceCriteria: JSON.Options sets Encoder = JavaScriptEncoder.Create(UnicodeRanges.All); serializing HTML-significant characters (<, >, &) still escapes them.
Serializing a non-ASCII string (e.g. "中文") via JSON.Serialize emits the characters verbatim, not \u4e2d\u6587 escapes (unit test).
JSON.Indented produces WriteIndented output that otherwise reuses JSON.Options settings (unit test).
UnknownFailureReasonJsonConverter is registered on JSON.Options; a FailureReason round-trip (known and unknown values) is value-identical to the pre-change representation (golden-master unit test).
dotnet build is clean (TreatWarningsAsErrors) and dotnet test for the affected server projects is green.
tasks.output: packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/Infrastructure/JSON.cs updated (encoder + Indented); promoted shared FailureReason converter type; new unit tests for encoder/indented/round-trip.
tasks.notes: ApprovalFeedbackStatusJsonConverter is attribute-based ([JsonConverter] on ApprovalFeedback.cs:6) and works under any options instance, so it needs no change. Do not delete WorkflowQuerier.RunJsonOptions here — that happens in T-003 once the converter is available on the facade.

tasks.title: Wire HTTP API and SignalR global JSON options to the unified facade
tasks.spec: specs/json-serialization/spec.md#HTTP API layer reuses the unified options for all responses
tasks.description: Register Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.Json.JsonOptions (SerializerOptions = JSON.Options) in MohistServiceRegistration.ConfigureMohistServices, and chain .AddJsonProtocol(o => o.PayloadSerializerOptions = JSON.Options) onto the existing services.AddSignalR() call so every outbound API response and both hubs (/hubs/runner, /hubs/events) serialize through the non-ASCII-preserving encoder. No per-route or per-call options overrides.
acceptanceCriteria: An API endpoint whose response payload contains Chinese text (e.g. an issue title) emits verbatim characters in the body with no \uXXXX escapes (integration test).
An error response from the unhandled-exception middleware whose message contains non-ASCII text emits verbatim characters (integration test).
A SignalR hub push whose payload contains non-ASCII text delivers verbatim characters to the client (integration test).
No response helper (Results.Ok/Results.Json, ApiResults.*, exception middleware) overrides the encoder with a locally constructed options instance.
dotnet test for the server project is green.
tasks.output: packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/Infrastructure/Hosting/MohistServiceRegistration.cs updated (global Http.Json.JsonOptions + AddSignalR().AddJsonProtocol); new integration tests for API and hub non-ASCII output.
tasks.notes: Also satisfies specs/json-serialization/spec.md#SignalR hubs reuse the unified options and specs/http-api/spec.md#API responses preserve non-ASCII characters verbatim. HTTP and SignalR wiring are intentionally one task (issue Bucket D — 2 global registrations off the same facade); splitting a one-line wiring each would be technical-step over-splitting.

tasks.title: Eliminate local JsonSerializerOptions fields and converge business serialization to the facade
tasks.spec: specs/json-serialization/spec.md#Server exposes a single JSON serialization entry point
tasks.description: Replace every local static readonly JsonSerializerOptions field and the inline new(JsonSerializerDefaults.Web) in Api/RunnerRoutes.cs with JSON.Options (or JSON.Indented for human-readable files such as ConfigService), following the design migration audit table. Middle-layer shared options (AgentSessionJson.JsonOptions, CloudEvent.JsonOptions, VariableBundle.JsonOptions, WorkflowYamlSerializer.JsonOptions, WorkflowVariableJson.Options, the *EventSerializer fields) become thin delegators to JSON.Options or are deleted where file-local. Switch the ~40 default-argument JsonSerializer.Serialize/Deserialize call sites (Workflow/Grains, Sessions, ConfigService, Label, Project, Api/LogsRoutes, etc.) to JSON.Serialize/JSON.Deserialize or to passing JSON.Options.
acceptanceCriteria: A ripgrep over packages/server/src excluding Infrastructure/JSON.cs returns zero matches for `new JsonSerializerOptions(`.
Every JsonSerializer.Serialize/Deserialize call in packages/server/src passes JSON.Options, JSON.Indented, or an options instance sourced from JSON.* (grep audit verification).
Enum-as-string representation and AgentSessionStore / session-state JSON are byte/value-identical to pre-change (golden-master tests where the type has a custom converter).
The one previously inline options in Api/RunnerRoutes.cs now uses JSON.Options.
dotnet test Mohist.sln is fully green, including all pre-existing serialization-related specs.
tasks.output: Local JsonSerializerOptions fields removed/delegated across Workflow, Sessions, Issue, Project, Events, Api, Storage; default-arg call sites switched to JSON.*; existing tests still pass.
tasks.notes: Depends on T-001 because the converter-bearing fields (WorkflowQuerier.RunJsonOptions, AgentSessionJson) can only reference JSON.Options once UnknownFailureReasonJsonConverter is registered on the facade. Independent of T-002 (transport wiring) — business-code options and transport wiring can proceed in parallel. Audit table is in openspec/changes/issue-218/design.md.

tasks.title: End-to-end verification of non-ASCII serialization across all surfaces
tasks.spec: specs/http-api/spec.md#API responses preserve non-ASCII characters verbatim
tasks.description: Human-verified end-to-end confirmation that non-ASCII (Chinese) appears verbatim everywhere after the convergence. Run a full dotnet test Mohist.sln, confirm the source-grep guard (no local options outside the facade), and manually exercise a running server+runner: create/view an issue with a Chinese title, a workflow with Chinese variables, and a runner event stream — confirming API responses, SignalR hub pushes, and persisted JSON (config/artifact/session) are readable Chinese. Also confirm backward compatibility: JSON persisted before the change still deserializes correctly.
acceptanceCriteria: Manual: an issue with a Chinese title — GET via API returns readable Chinese, and the hub event push is readable Chinese.
Manual: a Chinese workflow variable persists to SQLite and round-trips back as readable Chinese.
Manual: runner event stream and a persisted artifact/log containing Chinese are readable.
dotnet test Mohist.sln is fully green, including all pre-existing serialization-related specs.
Confirmed via grep: no `new JsonSerializerOptions(` outside Infrastructure/JSON.cs in packages/server/src.
Confirmed: persisted JSON written before the change (escaped or verbatim) still deserializes to equal values with no migration step.
tasks.output: Verification report: each acceptance criterion checked off against a running server+runner, with full green dotnet test Mohist.sln and the source-grep guard confirmed.
tasks.notes: HITL because the manual checks require a running server + runner and human judgment on readable Chinese rendering. Automated tests already live in T-001/T-002/T-003; this is the integration gate, not a test task. Also covers specs/json-serialization/spec.md#Deserialization stays backward-compatible with persisted JSON.
